deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page and nothing to reconstruct. The folio is a handwritten copy of entries from a second-hand bookseller's list: 'Kösslingsche Buchhandlung in Leipzig, Antiquarisches Anzeige-Blatt 1855, No. 14'. It lists three Laplace items with prices in Saxon Reichsthaler (rthlr) and Neugroschen (ngr), where 1 Thlr = 30 Ngr after 1840.

(1) Laplace, Traité de Mécanique céleste, 5 vols. in quarto ('4°'), with figures ('av. figs.'), Paris 1799–1825, bound in what appears to be 'Ppbde.' (Pappbände, boards): 12 Thlr 15 Ngr, i.e. 375 Ngr.

(2) The same work, vols. I–III sold separately, 'P[aris] 1799', Ppbde.: 7 Thlr 15 Ngr, i.e. 225 Ngr. The note in parentheses reads: 'Der erste Band hiervon etwas wasserfleckig, sonst ganz gut erhalten' (the first volume somewhat water-stained, otherwise quite well preserved).

(3) Laplace, Exposition du Système du Monde, 2nd edition ('É. II'), quarto ('4.'), Paris an VII (1798/99): 1 Thlr 15 Ngr, i.e. 45 Ngr.

The note documents interest, by Riemann or someone in his circle, in acquiring Laplace's celestial mechanics in 1855. 1855 is the year of Gauss's death and the period of Riemann's Göttingen lectures on mathematical physics. The page has no derivations, so there is nothing to reconstruct or verify mathematically. The handwriting may or may not be Riemann's own; I am unsure.
errors: No mathematical errors, since the page contains no mathematics.

Bibliographic imprecision: vols. I–III are dated 'P. 1799', but only vols. I–II of the Mécanique céleste appeared in 1799 (an VII); vol. III appeared in 1802 (an XI). This may be the catalogue's own simplification.
The full set's dates 1799–1825 are correct: vol. IV appeared in 1805, and vol. V in parts 1823–1825.

results.what: Bookseller's catalogue excerpt listing Laplace's Traité de Mécanique céleste (complete set and vols. I–III) and Exposition du Système du Monde (2nd ed.) with prices, Leipzig 1855
results.usually_credited_to: n/a (Laplace is the author of the works listed)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a copied antiquarian book-sale listing with no mathematical content. It is mildly interesting biographically (interest in Laplace's celestial mechanics around 1855), but Riemann's familiarity with Laplace is well known and unsurprising.

checkable.asserts: Price of the complete 5-volume set, 12 Thlr 15 Ngr, equals 375 Neugroschen at 30 Ngr per Thaler.
Price of vols. I–III, 7 Thlr 15 Ngr, equals 225 Neugroschen.
Vols. I–III cost 3/5 of the full set, the same proportion as 3 of 5 volumes.
Price of the Exposition du Système du Monde, 1 Thlr 15 Ngr, equals 45 Neugroschen.

transcription_corrections: 'Kössling'sche' — the manuscript reads 'Kösslingsche' (written as 'Kössling sche', without an apostrophe).
'Antiquarisches Anzeige Blatt' — the manuscript reads 'Antiquarisches Anzeige-Blatt' (Anzeigeblatt).
'4 av. figrs.' — reads '4. av. figs.', where '4' denotes quarto format (4°).
'Hpfbde.' — the binding abbreviation looks more like 'Ppbde.' (Pappbände, boards); the reading is uncertain.
'12 r 15 ngr' — the currency sign is the Reichsthaler abbreviation (rthlr/ℛ), i.e. '12 Thlr 15 Ngr'; likewise for '1 r 15 ngr'.
'E. II 4. Paris VII' — read as 'É. II, 4°, Paris [an] VII', i.e. 2nd edition, quarto, Paris year VII of the Republican calendar (1798/99).
'Mécanique céleste' — the manuscript's spelling looks like 'Mécanique céleste' with somewhat irregular letterforms; the content is unambiguous.
